fact_previews: Quantum WebGL is a project aimed at porting the QuantumGL software to the Web (HTML5/WebGL).
Henning Dekant is the creator of the Quantum WebGL project.
The project has received CA$ 8,111 in pledges from 20 backers.
The funding period for the Quantum WebGL project was from June 3, 2015, to August 2, 2015.

fact_previews: QuantumGL is a software tool used to create visualizations of the dynamics of electron orbital states.
The old QuantumGL program code is no longer maintained and has become obsolete.
The Windows binary version of QuantumGL can still be executed, but the Mac OSX version no longer works.
The Mac OSX version of QuantumGL cannot be compiled with the current version of Apple's development tools.
QuantumGL is open source, which allows for overcoming the hurdles of its obsolescence.

fact_previews: The QuantumGL tool will be available under the same open license as the original, ensuring that the full source code, including enhancements and modernizations, is accessible for anyone to use.
The project will invite other programmers to contribute modifications and will help coordinate and distribute their contributions.
The project will maintain backwards compatibility with examples from the original books.
The QuantumGL tool will be a web resource, allowing it to be used whenever quantum mechanics is taught or illustrated online.
The project aims to engage Open Source programmers, but does not expect serious coding to go financially unrewarded.
